proposals.before: Hence when Wei Qing and Huo Qubing went beyond the passes, a thousand companies did not return; when the Second Division entered the desert, a hundred hosts collapsed in surrender; Li Guang was defeated at the vanguard, Li Ling lost at the rear—the rest fled north in numbers beyond counting.
proposals.after: Hence when Wei Qing and Huo Qubing went beyond the passes, a thousand companies did not return; when the General of Ershi entered the desert, a hundred hosts collapsed in surrender; Li Guang was defeated at the vanguard, Li Ling was lost at the rear; the rest fled in defeat in numbers beyond counting.
proposals.reason: 貳師 is Li Guangli's title, the General of Ershi, not a military unit called the Second Division; 奔北 means to flee in defeat, not to flee north.

proposals.before: Hence when Wei Qing and Huo Qubing went beyond the passes, a thousand companies did not return; when the Second Division entered the desert, a hundred hosts collapsed in surrender; Li Guang was defeated at the vanguard, Li Ling lost at the rear—the rest fled north in numbers beyond counting.
proposals.after: Thus, when Wei Qing and Huo Qubing campaigned beyond the passes, a thousand companies failed to return; when the General of Ershi entered the desert, a hundred formations surrendered at once. Li Guang was defeated in the vanguard and Li Ling was lost in the rear; the others who fled in defeat were beyond counting.
proposals.reason: 貳師 is the General of Ershi, Li Guangli's title; 奔北 is the idiom for fleeing in defeat rather than a literal northward movement.

decisions.reason: The source uses 貳師 as Li Guangli's established military title and 奔北 as the idiom for flight after defeat; both literal renderings in the proposal are therefore required.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 貳師入漠，百旅頓降；其餘奔北，不可勝數

decisions.reason: The idiomatic revision accurately identifies the General of Ershi and renders 奔北 as fleeing in defeat while preserving the sentence's parallel military examples.
